## A second, distinct cause with the same loss shape — container restart, not background-wait

This card is about `os-dev` seats stalling under background wait. Today produced a **different** mechanism with an identical outcome, and the distinction is worth having on the card because a fix aimed only at the wait would not have caught it.

**Two separate losses from the `domain:engine` seat, 2026-08-26:**

| | cause | what was at risk |
|---|---|---|
| ~09:00Z | the stall this card describes — 3 seats, no activity for ~6h | 1 commit + 1206 uncommitted lines (#12068), 1 commit (#11671), nothing at all (#12393) |
| ~17:5xZ | **container restart killed 3 running seats mid-task** | 2 commits (#12559), 1 commit (#9276), **14 uncommitted files** (#11968) |

⭐ **The common factor is not the stall. It is that work lives only on container-local disk until the seat itself chooses to push** — and in both incidents every branch was still sitting at its base commit on origin while real work existed locally. A stalled seat and a killed seat are indistinguishable from origin: both look like "claimed, nothing pushed".

In the second incident nothing had reached origin at all, and one seat had **zero commits with 14 modified files** — the shape where a restart costs everything rather than the tail.

### What actually contained both

The same recovery, run by the PM from the surviving worktrees: `git rev-list --count <base>..HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain` per worktree, then push the commits and commit the uncommitted work under a message that says plainly it is **NOT REVIEWED, NOT VERIFIED**. Both times that was a judgement call made *after* the loss, not a mechanism.

### The cheap mitigation this suggests

A seat that pushes its branch **early and often** — even a `wip` commit at first meaningful progress — converts both failure modes from "everything lost" into "the last few minutes lost". Nothing about the current contract asks for that; it asks for a push at PR time. Two incidents in one shift, six seats affected, is the argument for moving it earlier.

⚠️ And a note for whoever writes the fix: **a background-wait watchdog would not have fired on the second incident.** The seats were not stalled — they were working, and then they were gone. The detector has to be "unpushed work exists on a branch whose seat is no longer alive", not "no activity for N minutes".

Recorded from the `domain:engine` PM seat; card not claimed, no labels changed. The per-card records are on #12068 / #11671 / #12393 and #12559 / #9276 / #11968, and §7 of seat post #6367.
